text:
maria_support: FYI acme reported weird behaviour on embeddings: a mix of unexpected cache misses and some entries returning 1024-dim vectors when their consumer expects 768. customer says this started after they toggled to 'text-embed-3-small' last week. logs attached.

acme_bob: yes, we saw spiky latency and then some vectors that don't match our downstream model dim -> failing prod checks. notably shipment 14:22 UTC had a bunch of misses, then a few hits returning 1024 dims.

maria_support: Repro steps from customer: 1) call /embeddings with model=text-embed-3-small 2) batch payloads of mixed lengths via our client (they use 8K batch window) 3) occasionally get vectors with 1024 dims. they suspect cache prefix reuse when model variants change.

alex_ml: sounds like a cache keying problem. do we include model variant + quantization + dim in the cache key today? last I recall keys were tenant + prefix + model_name.

sam_runtime: currently cache key = tenant_id + prefix + embedding_model_name (e.g. text-embed-3). we had omitted explicit dimension and quant flag for backward compat. that could explain collisions if model family surfaces different dims.

ashley_oncall: tagging me to check if any recent rollout changed model naming or aliasing that would collapse keys. @ci-bot can you surface recent deploys touching emb-cache or model routing in the last 48h? :eyes:

ci-bot: deploys touching emb-cache-service: 1850000001 (hotfix: cache metrics), 1850002500 (model-router: alias support), 1850004000 (batcher: reorder fixes).

maria_support: customer also provided a short server log excerpt showing two writes to the same cache key ~150ms apart with different vector lengths. pasted below:

```
[2025-08-12T14:22:01Z] INFO write_cache key=acme:prefix:tx123 model=text-embed-3-small dim=768 ttl=3600
[2025-08-12T14:22:01Z] INFO write_cache key=acme:prefix:tx123 model=text-embed-3-large dim=1024 ttl=3600
```

acme_bob: we didn't change our tenant prefix. we only switched model alias from text-embed-3 -> text-embed-3-small, expecting aliasing to be transparent.

alex_ml: if two writes hit same key with different dims, downstream will read whichever wins. possible race during batching or alias resolution. also TTLs look same so not eviction.

sam_runtime: thinking through code: batcher groups requests, then cache prefetch + write on completion. race window exists when model alias resolution happens concurrently with a background model migration job that updates canonical model_name -> variant mapping. if batch uses resolved name sometimes and canonical name other times, keys mismatch. but logs show same key string, so alias resolution likely collapsed into the same key.

maria_support: customer suggests "prefix reuse" — they explicitly use prefix=acme:tenant-1 in calls. they expected the platform to also suffix model id so keys are isolated by model variant.

alex_ml: we should enforce cache key = tenant + prefix + model_id_hash + dim + quantflag. That would avoid cross-variant collisions even if prefix is identical.

ashley_oncall: can we confirm whether emb-cache write includes dimension currently? sam?

sam_runtime: quick grep: write path uses metadata.model_name only. dimension is inferred on read but not part of key. so yes, missing. also batch write path uses non-atomic multi-key set which can reorder under concurrency.

maria_support: customer is asking for repro steps they can run on their side. they want the exact request pattern that triggers the collision so they can verify after our fix.

sam_runtime: suggested repro we can give them: 1) send alternating calls A and B where A uses model alias that resolves to 768 dim, B uses alias resolving to 1024 dim but both share tenant prefix. 2) use high concurrency (50 workers) and small inter-call delay (10-30ms) 3) send in bursts with batcher enabled so server groups some into same batch. This should produce mixed writes to the same cache key if aliasing collapses.

acme_bob: we'll try that in staging tomorrow. ideally you push a canary fix so we can validate without their workaround.

alex_ml: low-risk fix: change cache key computation to include model fingerprint and embedding length. also add assertion on read: if stored vector length != expected, treat as miss and increment metric emb_cache_dim_mismatch.

sam_runtime: agree. I'll open a small PR to: - include model_hash and dim in key - make writes atomic per-key (single set) - add metric and a debug log when dim mismatch occurs.

sam_runtime: PR open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/emb-cache/pull/879 (WIP). contains key change in utils/keying.go and added metric.

maria_support: ETA on canary? customer is on a tight cadence for next-day validation.

sam_runtime: canary to staging within 3 hours, prod canary in 12-24 after smoke. will flag if risky.

ci-bot: pipeline status for PR 879: tests passing (unit), e2e queued.

alex_ml: note: adding dim to key will cause cache churn (misses) initially until old entries expire. recommend setting a temporary safeguard: on read, if mismatch detected, record and treat as miss but keep previous entry for short grace period to avoid immediate cold-start regressions. also communicate potential short-term latency spike to customer.

sam_runtime: will implement grace read path: if mismatch and age < 5m, try background re-compute and serve old if background recompute slow. plan in PR.

maria_support: relaying to acme: we'll deploy a staged fix that prevents collisions but may cause a short increase in misses for ~TTL window. want them to run repro after staging canary.

acme_bob: that works. also request a small tool: endpoint to dump cache keys for their tenant so they can inspect collisions. not necessary but helpful.

sam_runtime: exposing key dump is risky security-wise. we can provide an admin-only read for keys with tenant filter and redact values. ops/security sign-off needed.

ashley_oncall: ops + sec are fine with redacted listing for validated tenant requests. open support ticket and we'll enable for acme.

maria_support: Update: staging canary deployed at 1850006000. acme ran repro and reported initial misses as predicted but no dim collisions. they see emb_cache_dim_mismatch metric spike during rollout.

acme_bob: can confirm staging looks good — no 1024-dim returns anymore. thanks.

sam_runtime: started rolling canary to prod at 1850007500 with 10% traffic. monitoring emb_cache_dim_mismatch and p50/p95 latency.

ci-bot: prod canary deploy 1850007500 -> success for canary slice.

maria_support: customer validated in staging and asked for prod cutover. do we have an expected full rollout window and messaging?

sam_runtime: full rollout scheduled over next 2 hours, will throttle by region. we'll post update when 100% done. expected benign misses for old entries until TTL expiry (~1h).

maria_support: thanks team. I'll send acme a summary: cause (cache key omitted dim/model fingerprint -> alias collapse), action (keying changed + grace read + metric), expected behavior (temporary spike in misses, collisions resolved), repro to validate.

acme_bob: thanks everyone for quick turnaround :saved:

maria_support: closing thread after full rollout confirmation.

sam_runtime: rolled to 100% at 1850007890, metrics normalized, no new dim mismatch errors in last 10m.

maria_support: resolved from support side.
